n = 397

Binary search for largest low such that low^3 <= n.

low=0, high=1000001.

We need cube root of 397. 7^3 = 343 <= 397, 8^3 = 512 > 397. So low = 7.

Then loop difference from 1 to 7:
We want x^3 - y^3 = 397, x - y = difference. Let d = x - y. Then x^3 - y^3 = d(x^2 + xy + y^2) = d(3y^2 + 3dy + d^2). So n/d = 3y^2 + 3dy + d^2 → 3y^2 + 3dy + d^2 - n/d = 0 → y = [-3d + sqrt(9d^2 - 12(d^2 - n/d))]/6 = [-3d + sqrt(12 n/d - 3d^2)]/6. That matches the discriminant formula.

Check each d:

d=1: 397 % 1 = 0. n//1 = 397. discriminant = 12*397 - 3 = 4764 - 3 = 4761. sqrt(4761) = 69 (69^2 = 4761). numerator = 69 - 3 = 66. 66 % 6 = 0. y = 11. x = 12. Check: 12^3 - 11^3 = 1728 - 1331 = 397. Yes! So print "12 11".
